Q: [Vue warn]: Failed to resolve directive: bin A:

Happened to me. The mistake I made was that I registered, with app.directive(...), my directive after having app.mount('#app'). So it did not take in effect. The solution was to apply my global directive before mounting the app

Q: Why dictionaries, lists, tuples, range etc are considered data types in python rather than data structures A:

A data type is a sticker you put on a value. Some values are labelled int, some list, some dict.

A data structure is a way of organizing data. Some data is organized in lists, other in dictionaries.

dict or list (Python identifiers) refer to data types. They are labels put on values that help the interpreter determine what can and cannot be done with these values.

OTOH, "list" and "dictionary" (English words) refer to data structures. They are ways to organize data. A "list" is a sequence of values that can be quickly accessed with an index (other languages often call this "array"), and a "dictionary" is something like a bunch of key-value pairs cleverly arranged for fast access by the key (other languages sometimes call this "finite map" or something similar).

It just so happens (or Python arranges it in just such a way) that a value labelled list organizes subordinate data items in a list, and a value labelled dict organizes subordinate data items in a dictionary. As a result, the two notions (data type and data structure) sometines get muddled a bit.
